territorial_scope.description: Applies to paid election-related synthetic media communications in Utah, including online communications viewable, audible, or accessible in the state.

evidence.quote: viewable, audible, or accessible in the state

summary.short: Amends Utah election code to require disclosure labels and tamper-evident provenance for paid political audio or visual communications containing AI-generated synthetic media, with court-imposed civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; adds an AI-use aggravating factor to criminal sentencing. Effective May 1, 2024; sentencing provision July 1, 2024.
summary.long: Section 1 creates Section 20A-11-1104, effective May 1, 2024. It applies to audio or visual communications that are paid for by a candidate campaign committee, political action committee, political issues committee, political party, or a person using a contribution; that are intended to influence voting for or against a candidate or ballot proposition in an election or primary in the state; and that contain synthetic media. Audio containing synthetic audio media must include spoken statements of the words 'Contains content generated by AI' at the beginning and end. Visual communications must display specified wording throughout each portion containing synthetic media, varying by whether the content is video, image, or both. Creators or sponsors who publish such online communications viewable, audible, or accessible in the state must ensure embedded tamper-evident digital content provenance disclosing the initial author and creator, subsequent editors, and any use of generative artificial intelligence. In a civil action to enforce the section, a court may impose a civil penalty not to exceed $1,000 per violation. A creator excludes a person that solely provides the technology used. Compliance does not exempt a person from other applicable civil or criminal liability. Section 2 creates Section 76-3-203.18, effective July 1, 2024, under which the sentencing judge or the Board of Pardons and Parole may consider intentional or knowing use and material assistance of an artificial intelligence system as an aggravating factor in criminal offenses.

notes: This is the enacting bill text itself; no session law number or enrolment history appears in the document, so the 2024 year comes from registry metadata. No legal_basis, amends, repeals or enacted_by_bill relation is stated. Section 1 is effective 05/01/24 and Section 2 is effective 07/01/24, consistent with Section 3(1) and 3(2). Subsection 4(c) says 'if the video includes synthetic audio media but not synthetic visual media' for audio-only content; coded as written. Subsection 5 switches from 'communication' to 'advertisement' without defining the latter. Subsection 6(a) provides a civil action 'by a person to enforce this section' with a court-imposed penalty; the text does not say who collects it.
